category_title: Preschoolers who cry when encountering perceived difficult tasks
minimal_context: Zeke is working on a fine motor bead-stringing activity at the Art center.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Zeke, here are the small beads and string for your art project.

STUDENT: (Whines softly) I can't put the string in.

TUTOR: Keep trying to push it through.

STUDENT: (Whines louder) It's too hard!

TUTOR: Just give it another try.

STUDENT: (Cries loudly and walks away from the table)

options.A: Terminate the task demands and remove the bead-stringing materials from the table for 10 seconds.
options.B: Prompt Zeke to use a sensory ball if he is crying and walking away from the table.
options.C: Ask Zeke what he is trying to create with the beads and string during the activity.
options.D: Use a peer tutor and puppets to model the bead-stringing task and establish joint attention.
